subject: Clarify subscriber float, escrow and pass-through liability for reseller addendum
messages:
From: Katie Lin <katie.lin@cloudmerchant.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudmerchant.com
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subscriber float / escrow handling for reseller addendum

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this on. As we move toward finalizing the reseller addendum (Marketplace/Partner Paper), two items that keep coming up on our end:

1) Subscriber float / settlement timing: our billing system bills customers at T+0 but marketplace settlements to resellers can lag. We need to document who carries chargeback/charge dispute exposure during the float window and whether Redwood will accept liability for chargebacks attributable to your hosted API usage during that period or if CloudMerchant will hold a short-term escrow.

2) Escrow / wire instructions: if CloudMerchant must hold funds pending settlement resolution, we need Redwood's operations wiring details and a short legal statement on permitted uses of the escrow (chargebacks only, not general operating expenses).

Attached are our suggested redlines and our escrow template for review. Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to:
- accept a 30-day settlement window with a capped escrow holdback equal to 2x expected monthly chargebacks, OR
- alternatively, act as payer-of-record for customer refunds within 14 days and invoice CloudMerchant for net settlements monthly?

We'd like to keep the timeline tight — target signature within 2 weeks if possible.

Appreciate any clarifications so we can present to procurement/legal on Friday.

Best,
Katie Lin
Head of Partnerships, CloudMerchant
[katie.lin@cloudmerchant.com]

Attachments: CloudMerchant_MSA_redlines.docx (docx), Escrow_Instructions.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Katie Lin <katie.lin@cloudmerchant.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subscriber float / escrow handling for reseller addendum

Katie —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick read-through and proposed next steps from our side:

- Legal (Irene) to review CloudMerchant_MSA_redlines.docx and flag any pass-through/indemnity language that creates open-ended liability.
- Partnerships (Ben) to confirm operational impact of acting as payer-of-record vs. escrow model and to surface expected monthly chargeback ranges so we can size any cap.
- My team will prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) with a target signature timeline and go/no-go decision points for escrow vs payer-of-record.

Prelim view: Redwood is open to a 30-day settlement window with a small capped escrow, but we need clarity on what chargeback types are included (fraud, refunds for service interruptions, tax adjustments, etc.). If CloudMerchant requires Redwood to be payer-of-record for refunds within 14 days, we will likely ask for additional credit protections (invoice holdback or a short-term credit line).

Irene — looping you in to review the redlines (particularly sections: pass-through of taxes, indemnity carveouts, and escrow use restrictions).
Ben — can you run ops to estimate expected monthly chargebacks and any integration changes to our finance reconciler?

I'll drop the MAP and a proposed timeline by EOD.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

[attachment: MAP-v1.docx (draft mutual action plan)]

From: Legal - CloudMerchant <legal@cloudmerchant.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: katie.lin@cloudmerchant.com, procurement@cloudmerchant.com
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Subscriber float / escrow handling for reseller addendum

Hannah / team —

Appreciate the quick reply. Per internal review we pushed a few targeted redlines (attached). Highlights / asks:

- We moved to explicit language that CloudMerchant retains chargeback exposure for fraud-only items and that Redwood would accept refunds for operational service failures (uptime/availability) within 30 days.
- Requested carveout: CloudMerchant wants escrow funds to cover both chargebacks and tax adjustments (we've called these out in our template). Please confirm Redwood's position on taxes — will Redwood accept pass-through of tax liabilities tied to marketplace transactions or do you require CloudMerchant to remain the taxpayer-of-record?
- Escrow mechanics: we propose the following for speed:
  * CloudMerchant wires to a mutually agreed escrow account within 5 business days of invoiced settlement shortfalls
  * Redwood provides an ops escrow release form for chargeback claims with a 14-day dispute window
  * Standard audit rights for CloudMerchant to verify Redwood's usage logs relevant to disputed transactions

We attached CloudMerchant_MSA_redlines.docx and Escrow_Instructions.pdf. We are flexible on the cap, but need a concrete number to present to procurement. Proposed cap: 1.5x average monthly net refunds (we provided a three-month sample in the doc).

Can Irene propose precise redlines that limit Redwood's exposure to quantifiable events (service credits, tax adjustments, verified fraud)? Also confirm what operational data Redwood can provide to support escrow releases (billing tokens, request/response IDs, and a daily settlement manifest).

Thanks — we are pushing procurement to close this week pending your legal/ops alignment.

— CloudMerchant Legal

Attachments: CloudMerchant_MSA_redlines.docx (docx), Escrow_Instructions.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: katie.lin@cloudmerchant.com, procurement@cloudmerchant.com
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Subscriber float / escrow handling for reseller addendum — recommended approach and owners

Team — forwarding CloudMerchant's redlines and escrow template (see thread). Key recommendations before we reply:

1) Liability scoping (Irene): propose limiting Redwood liability to operational failures (service availability/incorrect billing attributable to our runtime) and verified fraud where we can demonstrate platform causation. Exclude broad tax liabilities — CloudMerchant should remain taxpayer-of-record for their marketplace sales, with Redwood providing reasonable assistance for tax audits.

2) Escrow mechanics (Ben + Marissa Ops/Finance): accept 30-day settlement window with a capped escrow — recommend we propose a conservative cap at 1.25x monthly net refunds for first 3 months while we observe actual chargeback rates. Ops must confirm we can produce the daily settlement manifest and a request/response ID dump for dispute support. If we cannot meet that data output, we default to payer-of-record model with a 14-day refund SLA and an invoice holdback.

3) Process & timing (Hannah): propose the following timeline:
  - Tue AM: Irene to send redline counter with explicit carveouts (pass-through taxes: NO; escrow permitted uses: chargebacks & verified tax adjustments only).
  - Wed: Ben/Marissa to confirm wiring template and provide a reconciliation sample (3 months).
  - Thu: Send executed MAP and proposed final redlines back to CloudMerchant.

Please put suggested contract language inline and keep the reply tight — procurement is ready to approve if we give a definitive path.
